headline: Iran war, oil and trade talks dominate a week capped by the U.S. vote
summary: Oil hovered near six-month highs as Qatar mediated Iran talks, and the Bank of Canada raised rates while new data showed the economy stalling. Canada-U.S. trade talks revived, with Trump calling a deal very close, while Ontario's deficit grew to $16.9 billion. The week ends with record early voting ahead of Tuesday's U.S. midterms and Ottawa's budget on Thursday.

top.headline: Oil slides 3% to about US$110 as Iran–Qatar talks continue
top.what: Oil prices fell in Monday trading as Iran and Qatari mediators kept talking and reports said Trump wants to give diplomacy more time before deciding on new strikes.
top.why: Oil above US$110 is the main force behind higher inflation in Canada and the U.S., and it pushed the Bank of Canada into a rate hike last week.

top.headline: Trump says Canada deal 'very close' after call with Carney
top.what: A day after a call with Prime Minister Mark Carney, Donald Trump told reporters the two countries have the outline of a trade deal, though no terms or tariff relief have been announced.
top.why: Ontario sells most of its steel and auto output to the U.S., and the province says steel exports there have fallen by more than half since 2024.

top.headline: Midterm eve: Trump speaks in Washington as early vote passes 54M
top.what: On the eve of Tuesday's midterms, Trump gives his closing speech in Washington while Democrats rally in key states, with polls favouring Democrats for the House and the Senate a toss-up.
top.why: A Democratic Congress could check Trump's tariffs and war powers, while Republican control would give him a freer hand for the next two years.

top.headline: Economy stalls in August, two days after Bank of Canada's hike
top.what: Statistics Canada says the economy was flat in August and probably shrank 0.1% in September, a weak backdrop for the Bank of Canada's first rate increase since 2023.
top.why: The data shows the bank raising rates into a stalling economy, a tough trade-off that makes its next moves less predictable.

top.headline: Ontario's deficit swells to $16.9 billion as tariffs delay balanced budget
top.what: Finance Minister Peter Bethlenfalvy's fall economic statement projects a record $16.9-billion deficit this year and $36 billion over three years, pushing a balanced budget beyond 2028.
top.why: Bigger deficits mean more provincial borrowing and interest costs, which can squeeze future spending on health, schools and transit.

top.headline: Poilievre lists budget demands as Thursday's federal budget nears
top.what: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre wrote to Prime Minister Mark Carney asking for fuel tax relief and spending cuts in the budget Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne tables Thursday, Nov. 5.
top.why: The budget sets federal taxes, benefits, defence spending and borrowing during the trade war.

top.headline: Kherson truce ends as Russian strikes leave Ukrainians without power
top.what: A short humanitarian ceasefire around occupied Oleshky in Kherson region expired Sunday night, as Russian strikes on the power grid kept outages in place across Ukraine.
top.why: Talks in early November could be the first real test of a ceasefire path since early this year.

top.headline: Final count leaves Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats, short of a majority
top.what: Israel faces weeks of coalition talks after final results gave neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Gadi Eisenkot's a 61-seat majority, and Likud claimed the vote was stolen.
top.why: Who governs Israel will shape whether the war with Iran escalates or winds down.
